newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-LAWYER SAID DRUGS PLANTED ON MARADONA'S MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAWYER SAID DRUGS PLANTED ON MARADONA'S MANAGER.

text.p: A lawyer for Guillermo Coppola, Argentine soccer star Diego Maradona's manager, said on Monday that cocaine was planted in the home of his client.

Coppola was arrested two weeks ago in a police raid that found a pound (500 grams) of cocaine in his luxury apartment. He was charged with possession of drugs for sale and could face up to 20 years in prison.
His lawyer Mariano Cuneo Libarona said Coppola was wrongly indicted because the drugs were planted in his apartment.

Testimony given in court on Monday by two women showed "that the drugs supposedly confiscated in Guillermo Coppola's house were put there to implicate him in a criminal case," the lawyer said in a statement.
The two women, Julieta Lavalle and Samantha Farjat, reportedly told a judge that another woman involved in the case, Natalia De Negri, could have planted the cocaine in Coppola's apartment.
But federal judge Hernan Bernasconi, who indicted Coppola, said "absolutely nothing changes in the case with this" and said the women's testimony was part of a "defence strategy."
The women regularly attended parties thrown by Coppola.
Maradona's brother-in-law, Gabriel Esposito and ex-soccer player Alberto Tarantini were also arrested but have only been sentenced to drug rehabilitation. De Negri is Tarantini's girlfriend.
Maradona is due to give evidence on Tuesday in the case, which has gripped Argentina's attention for more than two weeks with continuous new developments.
Coppola has told a judge that after he left his home during a party a few days before the police raid, Maradona and three women partied there until late the next day.
